---
title: "gg_get_legend"
---
<br>
```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "> "
)
```

```{r setup}
library(saferGG)
```
<br>

### Datasets

```{r}
obs1 <- data.frame(time = 1:20, group = rep(c("CLASS_1", "CLASS_2"), times = 10), stringsAsFactors = TRUE) # small dataset with a categorical column
```
<br>

### Dataset info

```{r}
utils::head(obs1) # head of the dataset
```
<br>

### Simple example

```{r}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot() + ggplot2::geom_point(data = obs1, mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = time, fill = group)) # ggplot with a legend
gg_get_legend(ggplot_built = ggplot2::ggplot_build(p))
```
<br>

### NULL result when no legend in the ggplot

```{r}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot() + ggplot2::geom_point(data = obs1, mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = time)) # ggplot without legend
gg_get_legend(ggplot_built = ggplot2::ggplot_build(p))
```
<br>

### Use with ggplot2::grid.arrange() (typical use case: one single legend for several plots)

```{r, fig.height = 6}
p1 <- ggplot2::ggplot() + ggplot2::geom_point(data = obs1, mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = time, color = group))
legend <- gg_get_legend(ggplot_built = ggplot2::ggplot_build(p1))
gridExtra::grid.arrange(grid::nullGrob(), p1, legend, layout_matrix = rbind(c(1, 2), c(3, 3)), widths = c(1, 4), heights = c(4, 1))
```
<br>
